item.description: Edgerunners join us for an introductory Cyberpunk RED one-shot campaign. We embrace the chaotic, the quirky, and the dangerously stylish street-level action. We’re all about having a blast, taking big risks, and creating unforgettable memories on the neon-lit streets of Night City. Players aged 16 and up are welcome to play. This is a safe space for all, including LGBTQIA+ and Neurodiverse folk. Players will be playing the one shot: Red Chrome Cargo: A trusted Fixer offers your crew a dangerous mission. A client with deep pockets wants another Fixer embedded in the local “government” killed. It pays 9,000eb per person and comes with an operational budget of 1,000eb each to spend on equipment – remember, the Fixer expects any non-expendable gear purchased with that 1,000eb to be returned when the mission is finished. item.title: The Maine - The Tour Next Door — Fri Nov 13, 7:30 PM — The Wellmont Theater
item.description:
The Maine are a thrilling aberration in the unruly world of modern rock music: a band whose following has organically grown to unprecedented heights nearly 20 years into their career, thanks to the raw emotional power of their cathartic breed of alt-rock. In a bold new pinnacle for the Arizona-bred five-piece—vocalist John O’Callaghan, guitarists Jared Monaco and Kennedy Brock, bassist Garrett Nickelsen, drummer Pat Kirch—their tenth studio album Joy Next Door arrives as their most high-concept work yet while doubling down on The Maine’s singular balance of sonic ferocity and unflinching sincerity. Completed just before embarking on their biggest tour to date (the 2026 headline run I Love You But…I Chose The Maine), the result is a glorious testament to a band whose unbridled passion only burns brighter with time. item.title: Newburgh Beacon Hudson Hike — Sun Nov 15, 8:30 AM
item.description: Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! Join us for this point to point hike, the next in our Hudson River Series from one of the spots where we previously left off! There is a whole lot to see when walking though along trails, back streets, and towns on the Hudson River. This time, much of the route will be the sort of proposed extension of the Highlands Trail from where it currently terminates at Cornwall on Hudson to Beacon. We'll meet at the Memorial Park parking lot at Fishkill Ave and Robert Cahill intersection. From there, we'll shuttle with as few cars as possible to our beginning point in Cornwall on Hudson. We'll pass through a little town park at the beginning, and then follow back streets to Dock Hill and the Highlands Trail route. item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Nov 18, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.title: Silent Book Club Montclair — Wed Nov 18, 5:00 PM — Montclair Public Library
item.description:
At Silent Book Club® there's no assigned reading. SBC members gather in bars, cafés, bookstores, libraries, and online to read together in quiet camaraderie. All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction... it's BYOBook.
Did you love silent reading time in school? Are you more of an introvert that loves books, but doesn't want to jump into a discussion group? Are you looking to read more, but struggle to sit down and just DO IT? If you answered 'yes' to any of these, you might like Silent Book Club! Each month, we meet around Montclair and enjoy each other's company with a book of our own choosing.
Registration is required. Location TBD.
Please be advised this book club will be meeting at a public location and therefore cannot guarantee a quiet reading environment. This book club is best for readers who enjoy a coffeeshop ambiance (low chatter, music, outside noise, etc.) or those who prefer to read with headphones.
Source: Libcal Bccls 1030

Hosted by Kim Marsh, The Open Book Company What are you avoiding when it comes to your writing? Writers of all genres, interests, and experience levels are welcome to join this two-part reflective workshop.
We’ve all experienced shame, self-doubt, and fear when it comes to sharing our words with others.
What does it feel like to name those emotions and our own inner critics? What does it look like to examine what we may be avoiding because of it?

item.title: Civic Leadership and SEL: Lessons from NJ Changemakers with New Jersey Hall of Fame — Mon Dec 7, 4:30 PM — Online
item.description: Civic Leadership and SEL: Lessons from NJ Changemakers invites educators to explore how the powerful, personal stories of New Jersey Hall of Fame inductees can serve as catalysts for meaningful social-emotional learning and authentic civic engagement in today’s classrooms. By examining moments of courage, empathy, advocacy, and ethical decision-making in the lives of New Jersey leaders, educators will uncover practical ways to help students build self-awareness, social awareness, and a sense of agency. Drawing from the lives and legacies of Peter J. McGuire (Father of Labor Day), Dorothea Dix (mental health reformer), David Mixner (political activist, author, and playwright), and Clara Maass (public health pioneer), participants will analyze how these changemakers confronted injustice, advocated for vulnerable communities, and took action in times of social and public health crises—making abstract concepts such as fairness, wellness, and justice tangible and relevant for students. item.title: Eagle Rock Reservation — Fri Feb 5, 9:15 AM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.
We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.
Will will meet at: [https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1
If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.
Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.
**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**
